gaps.sentence: She works as ___ waitress during the summer holidays.
gaps.explanation: After 'as' and 'work as', jobs take a/an: work as a waitress.

gaps.sentence: I only need ___ few more minutes to finish.
gaps.explanation: 'A few minutes' = some minutes; 'few' alone would mean almost none.

gaps.sentence: I downloaded ___ MP3 file from the band's website.
gaps.explanation: 'MP3' is pronounced /em/, a vowel sound, so 'an'.

gaps.sentence: ___ books you left on my desk were really useful.
gaps.explanation: 'The books you left…' — the clause identifies which books.

gaps.sentence: ___ information you sent was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'The information you sent' — the clause defines it; information is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.

gaps.sentence: He demands ___ answer before the end of the day.
She gets up at six and watches ___ morning news.
gaps.explanation: 'The morning news' — a specific known broadcast, so 'the'.
